nodes.name: Atum → Shu/Tefnut → Geb/Nut → Osiris & Isis → Horus
nodes.notes: Egyptian royal king lists trace historical pharaohs directly from the Ennead and Horus through the Shemsu-Hor ('Followers of Horus'). Osiris placed in a chest/ark on the Nile was later compared by syncretists to Noah.

nodes.name: Thoth (Djehuty / Hermes) & King Saurid (Surid)
nodes.role: Egyptian Scribe of the Gods / Antediluvian Pyramid Builder
nodes.notes: Greco-Egyptian, Hermetic, Coptic, and Arabic histories explicitly identify Biblical Enoch (Idris) with Egyptian Thoth / Hermes Trismegistus and the antediluvian Egyptian King Saurid (Surid), who foresaw the Flood and built the Pyramids to preserve astronomy and sacred wisdom!

nodes.name: Menes / Narmer (1st Dynasty) & Baysar (Misrayim)
nodes.notes: Historical unifier of Egypt. Medieval Coptic/Arabic chronicles (al-Maqrizi) trace post-Flood Egyptian kings from Ham -> Baysar -> Misrayim (Mizraim), while Book of Jasher 14 recounts Rikayon establishing the royal title 'Pharaoh'!

nodes.name: Imhotep (Vizier of Djoser / 7-Year Famine)
nodes.era: Old Kingdom (3rd Dynasty) / Ptolemaic Famine Stela
nodes.notes: Master architect of the Step Pyramid and high priest of Heliopolis (On). The Sehel Island Famine Stela credits Imhotep with ending a 7-year Nile famine—frequently compared in cross-cultural lore with Joseph (Zaphenath-Paneah), who wed the daughter of the Priest of On!

nodes.name: Osarseph (Manetho) / Musaeus (Artapanus) / Bithiah & Adoniah
nodes.notes: Manetho preserves an Egyptian tradition of a Heliopolitan priest named Osarseph who took the name Moses; Artapanus calls Moses 'Musaeus' (teacher of Orpheus) and Egyptian 'Hermes', leading an expedition into Cush/Ethiopia — strikingly echoing Book of Jasher 72-76 where Moses rules Cush with Queen Adoniah!

nodes.name: Protogonos → Misor & Sydyk → Taaut (Thoth) & Chna (Canaan)
sources: Philo of Byblos / Sanchuniathon (via Eusebius Praep. Ev. I.10)
nodes.notes: Explicitly names Misor (direct cognate of Biblical Mizraim!) as brother of Sydyk (Righteousness, cf. Melchizedek) and father of Taaut (Egyptian Thoth, inventor of writing), alongside Chna (Canaan).
